original_title: Axially Chiral Sulfonic Acids for Atroposelective Synthesis of C–N Axially Chiral 1,2‐Diarylbenzimidazoles
title: Sulfonic acid catalysts for a chiral axis nobody usually bothers resolving
blurb: New axially chiral sulfonic acid organocatalysts cyclize o-phenylenediamines with aldehydes into 29 C-N axially chiral diarylbenzimidazoles at just 2.5 mol% loading. The reaction itself only gets to a modest 16:84 er, with a single recrystallization doing the heavy lifting up past 99:1.

original_title: A Stereocontrolled Synthesis of (4R)-1-Methyl-4-Propyl-L-Proline, the Amino Acid Fragment of Lincomycin
title: Getting to lincomycin's odd amino acid fragment, the hard way first
blurb: A stereoselective route turns commercial 4-hydroxy-L-proline into the 4R-methyl-propyl-proline piece that lincomycin needs, and they're upfront that two earlier routes failed before this one worked. Not a new antibiotic, just a cleaner way to make a piece of an old one, which still counts given how little else is in the pipeline.

original_title: Mechanocatalytic Upcycling of Diverse Plastic Wastes via an Fe/SiO 2 Catalyst
title: Grinding mixed plastic waste into hydrogen and methane
blurb: Ball-milling polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, polyester, and mixtures of all four against an Fe/SiO2 catalyst converts them to H2 and CH4 at near-100% conversion under mild conditions, with iron worn off the milling balls themselves anchoring onto the silica mid-run. Taking a mixed waste stream and not needing to sort it first is the actual selling point.

original_title: An Oxidative Twist to the Interrupted Pummerer Reaction: Unlocking Inaccessible Aryl Sulfonium Salts
title: A fluorine fix for the Pummerer reaction's sulfoxide problem
blurb: The interrupted Pummerer route to aryl sulfonium salts has always needed sulfoxides that are rarely sold and activators harsh enough to wreck functional group tolerance. Swapping in Selectfluor as the oxidant opens up sulfonium salts that were previously out of reach, a fix to the reagent problem rather than a new reaction, but apparently that's what's been bottlenecking people.

original_title: Guest-Mediated On-Surface Growth of 2D COF Heterobilayer for Synaptic Devices
title: Coronene holds the door open for COF-on-COF growth
blurb: Growing one covalent organic framework directly on top of another usually wrecks the bottom layer before the top one forms. Stuffing coronene guest molecules into the imine COF's pores stabilizes it long enough to redirect growth into a clean imine/boroxine heterobilayer, built with synaptic devices in mind.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Practical Reduction of Free Carboxylic Acids to Aldehydes with a Simple Silane
title: Turning carboxylic acids straight into aldehydes with cheap silane
blurb: Stopping a reduction at the aldehyde instead of overshooting to the alcohol is normally the hard part. This one does it with phenylsilane and potassium acetate, stoichiometric, mild conditions, one-pot compatible, and the mechanistic work points to a reduction pathway nobody had clocked before.

original_title: Automated Flow Synthesis of Combinatorial Protein‐Length Polyamide Libraries
title: Quintillion-compound polyamide libraries, now at protein length
blurb: Their flow platform could already spit out up to 10^18 sequence-defined polyamides per pooled mixture in under an hour, but it choked once chains got protein-length. Grafting the mixture-based approach onto automated flow peptide synthesis fixes that.

original_title: A Multi-Gram Synthesis of 7,12-Dibromo[7]helicene
title: A helicene nobody's made before, now in multigram batches
blurb: Ten steps to a never-before-reported 7,12-dibromo[7]helicene, with the bromines doing double duty as blocking groups to force regiocontrol at a late-stage Mallory photocyclization. Multigram output, but an earlier Mallory step elsewhere in the route is apparently the real bottleneck.

original_title: One Carbon Matters: Conformational Bending Stabilizes Ferroelectric Nematic Order and Enables Domain‐Modulated Antiferroelectric Smectic C Order
title: One CH2 swap decides ferroelectric or antiferroelectric
blurb: Swap the order of a methylene and an ether oxygen in the linker between the rigid core and the tail, same atoms, just rearranged, and you reshape how the molecule bends. That alone decides whether it stabilizes ferroelectric nematic order or tips into a domain-modulated antiferroelectric smectic C phase.

original_title: Photoinduced Direct N-Arylation of Nitroalkanes at Ambient Temperature via 1,2-Boronate Shift
title: Getting nitroalkanes, not just nitroarenes, to do photochemistry
blurb: Nitroalkanes have a nastier n to pi star transition than nitroarenes, which is why nobody had photoexcited one for a reductive coupling before. This one pairs photoexcited nitroalkanes with arylboronic acids via a 1,2-boronate shift to make N-aryl products at room temperature with no metal and no photocatalyst.

original_title: Asymmetric Total Synthesis of ent -Ailanthusin E
title: First asymmetric route to ent-ailanthusin E, starting from a cheap plant extract
blurb: Built from commercially available andrographolide rather than anything exotic. An iron-catalyzed MHAT cyclization nails two quaternary stereocenters at once with full diastereocontrol, a photoredox radical cascade closes the tetracyclic core, and it finishes with a one-pot sulfite ester cyclopropanation.

original_title: Photochemical Thio- and Selenoesterification of Aldehydes via C–H Bromination
title: Selenoesters from aldehydes, no photocatalyst required
blurb: Photochemical thioesterification of aldehydes has been done under photocatalysis before, but selenoesterification hadn't. This gets both from a simple C-H bromination step, turning aldehydes plus thiols or selenophenol straight into a range of thio- and selenoesters.

original_title: Early Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Single‐Photon Emission Computerized Tomography Detection of Breast Cancer With Netrin‐1‐Specific Molecular and Liposome Probes
title: A Netrin-1 probe spots tiny breast tumors, but the kidneys won't let go of it
blurb: A peptide built against the Netrin-1 biomarker, conjugated to a DOTA-like chelator, picks up small tumors by SPECT in a mouse triple-negative breast cancer model before anything would show up morphologically. The catch is kidney uptake so high it still dominates the signal 24 hours after injection.

original_title: ImmunoPET-guided TIM-3 theranostics enables dynamic visualization of adaptive immune escape and targeted radioimmunotherapy.
title: Watching tumors dodge the immune system in real time, via TIM-3 PET
blurb: Pairs a TIM-3-targeted immunoPET tracer with radioimmunotherapy aimed at the same target, using the imaging side to track adaptive immune escape as it happens rather than after the fact.

original_title: A Highly Active and Promiscuous Esterase for Amide Bond Synthesis under Aqueous Conditions
title: An esterase that's 8600x better at making amides than the old standard
blurb: They screened a panel of promiscuous acyltransferase enzymes and found SoEst12, a family VIII carboxylesterase that favors amide bond synthesis over hydrolysis in plain water. Kinetics put it up to 8600 times faster than PestE on a model reaction, the kind of gap that makes enzymatic amide coupling look genuinely usable instead of a curiosity.

original_title: Expedient Photochemical Synthesis of syn‐Ladderanes
title: syn-Ladderanes made in one photochemical step
blurb: Syn-ladderanes are the cubane-adjacent, absurdly strained hydrocarbons nobody's made more than a handful of examples of in decades. This runs ordinary 2-pyridones through a new photochemical cascade and gets 22 of them in a single step, 25-97% yield, including unsymmetrical ones you can diversify further. Simple feedstock for molecules that are usually miserable to touch.

original_title: Chemo- and Regioselective Dehydrogenative Allylic C–H Oxygenation of Ketones
title: An allylic C-H oxygenation that skips the directing-group dance
blurb: Oxidative allylic C-H functionalization is the usual shortcut to allylic ethers, but it typically needs precoordination and still gives messy selectivity. This one claims chemo- and regioselective control without that setup, which would open up more of the chemical space than current methods reach. Whether "general" survives beyond the showcase substrates is the open question.

original_title: Total Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of Cannalactone, a Noncanonical Strigolactone from Hemp
title: Hemp makes its own strigolactone, and now so does a flask
blurb: Strigolactones are the phytohormones that root parasites like Orobanche and Phelipanche key off to germinate near a host, and hemp apparently produces an unusual one called cannalactone. This paper does the total synthesis and runs the biological evaluation, relevant given some Phelipanche ramosa populations specifically target hemp.

original_title: Establishing Methyl 9‐Undecenoate as a Renewable Platform Molecule From Local Plant Oils for Catalytic Access to C 12 ‐Polymer Precursors
title: Methyl 9-undecenoate as the next plant-oil route to C12 polymer building blocks
blurb: Starting from methyl oleate, a common plant-oil derivative, they establish methyl 9-undecenoate as a renewable platform chemical and convert it catalytically into a range of C12 precursors for polyamides and polyesters. The pitch is a scalable, locally-sourced bio-based alternative to petrochemical monomers, assuming the catalytic steps hold up past the lab bench.

original_title: Quantitative proteomic approaches to studying redox post‐translational modifications in skeletal muscle
title: Tracking which cysteines muscle actually oxidizes, and how much
blurb: A review of mass-spec methods for mapping redox post-translational modifications on cysteine thiols in skeletal muscle, where reactive oxygen species double as signaling molecules rather than just damage. The useful part is the newer methods that quantify stoichiometry, not just which proteins get hit.

original_title: Expanding the Family of Co(III) Complexes With Exclusive Metal‐Centered Chirality: Application as an Enantioselective Selector in Voltammetric Sensor for Tyrosine Enantiomers
title: A cobalt complex that can tell your tyrosine enantiomers apart
blurb: They resolved a racemic Co(III) salicylaldehyde complex, built from cheap 1,2-phenylenediamine, into pure Λ and Δ forms using a chiral BINPHAT counterion and column chromatography, over 99% ee. The Λ form then works as an enantioselective selector in a voltammetric sensor for tyrosine enantiomers, a nice payoff for a complex made from unremarkable starting materials.

original_title: Efficient, Repeatable and Cost-effective 17O-Isotopic Labeling of Proline and Hydroxyproline for 17O-NMR Analyses
title: A cheaper way to oxygen-17 label proline for NMR
blurb: Cost-effective, repeatable routes to label the carboxylic oxygen of proline and hydroxyproline, plus their Fmoc derivatives, with 17O, some via mechanochemistry, for solid-state NMR studies of their local structure and dynamics. Not glamorous, but 17O labeling is usually the bottleneck for this kind of work, so a recipe you can actually repeat matters.

original_title: Position-Dependent Conformational Landscapes of Flavin–Tryptophan Pairs in Designed Magnetosensitive Protein Maquettes
title: Where you put the tryptophan decides how the radical pair behaves
blurb: In designed flavomaquette proteins, they map how flavin-tryptophan photoinduced electron transfer and the resulting spin-correlated radical pairs shift depending on where the tryptophan sits in the scaffold. A synthetic-biology stand-in for how the local environment tunes magnetically sensitive radical-pair chemistry, which is the mechanism everyone argues about for magnetoreception.

original_title: l -Altrosyl Donors: Synthesis, Glycosylation Reactivity, and Access to Disaccharide Fragments of Enterococcus faecium and Butyrivibrio fibrisolvens Glycans
title: Building the rare sugar L-altrose into bacterial glycan fragments
blurb: L-altrose turns up in the extracellular polysaccharides of several pathogens but is a pain to make. This route gets there from D-galactose via a galactofuranoside intermediate, regioselective C2/C3 protections, and a C5 inversion, then puts the resulting thioglycoside donors to work building disaccharide fragments from Enterococcus faecium and Butyrivibrio fibrisolvens glycans.

original_title: Chemogenetic dissection of the H2O2–salicylic acid feedback loop in PTI and ETI evolutionary conservation
title: One probe to watch H2O2 and salicylic acid argue in real time
blurb: A single fluorescent probe with two orthogonal reaction sites reads out hydrogen peroxide and salicylic acid at once in rice, without the two signals bleeding into each other. Fluorescence jumps 25-fold and 250-fold at 562 and 751 nm, with detection limits down to 96 and 24 nM, enough to actually watch the H2O2-SA feedback loop that runs plant immunity instead of inferring it from separate experiments on separate samples.

original_title: Optimisation of a dilute-and-shoot UHPLC-MS method for high-throughput urinary metabolomics
title: Urine prep that's literally just dilute and shoot
blurb: An optimized dilute-and-shoot extraction paired with untargeted UHPLC-MS, built to be fast enough for large cohorts rather than boutique metabolomics work. They validated it on an actual clinical cohort, which is the part urine metabolomics methods usually skip on the way to publication.

original_title: Heteronuclear Ru–Fe Dual Single-Atom Sites Anchored on Lanthanum Metal–Organic Framework Catalyzing the Base-Free Selective Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
title: Two metals, one MOF, no base needed for HMF to FDCA
blurb: A RuFe dual single-atom catalyst anchored on a lanthanum MOF pushes the biomass oxidation of HMF to FDCA, the monomer behind bio-based plastics, to nearly 99% yield in water. Base-free is the actual selling point, since skipping the base is what would make this cheaper to run than the usual route.

original_title: Trigonal Prismatic Coordination Field‐Induced d‐Orbital Splitting Enables σ Electron Activation for Efficient Polysulfide Conversion in Li–S Batteries
title: Why NbSe2 is good at shuttling polysulfides around
blurb: Using NbSe2 as a model catalyst, they trace how its trigonal prismatic coordination field splits the d-orbitals and opens sigma*-sigma and pi*-sigma electron transfer channels at the metal sites, which is what actually drives polysulfide conversion in Li-S batteries. More mechanism paper than working battery, but it's the kind of mechanism that tells you what to design toward next.

original_title: Cobalt Isolated Single-Atomic Sites for Iso-butane Direct Dehydrogenation with Robust Anti-Coke Deposition
title: A cobalt catalyst that dehydrogenates isobutane without choking on its own coke
blurb: Isolated single-atom Co sites hit 46% isobutane conversion and 90% selectivity to isobutene at 550°C, and ran 24 hours with no coke detected by TEM or Raman. Coking is usually what kills cheap-metal alternatives to Pt in this reaction, so a clean 24-hour run is the actual news here.

original_title: PharmaLogic Buys Lantheus' Springfield Site to Build First Transatlantic Radiopharmaceutical CDMO - GeneOnline
title: Lantheus sells a site, PharmaLogic builds a transatlantic radiopharma CDMO out of it
blurb: PharmaLogic bought Lantheus' Springfield facility to stitch together what it's calling the first transatlantic CDMO for radiopharmaceuticals. Real estate and capacity move, not science, but worth noting if you're tracking who'll actually have the manufacturing to back the next wave of radiotherapies.

original_title: In Situ Product Separation Suppresses Self‐Poisoning in 2‐Butanol Electrooxidation
title: Pulling the ketone out as you make it fixes 2-butanol electrooxidation
blurb: Swapping oxygen evolution for 2-butanol electrooxidation gets you hydrogen and methyl ethyl ketone together, but the MEK product normally poisons the reaction it came from. A PdAu/NF anode plus in situ product separation keeps the surface clean enough to sustain it. The self-poisoning fix is the actual contribution, not the alloy.

original_title: Precise Interlayer Ru─O─M Electronic Bridge Installation in Hydrotalcite‐Like Metal‐Organic Frameworks for Boosted Electrochemical Amine Oxidation
title: Wiring Ru to CoNi through oxygen bridges to make nitriles electrochemically
blurb: Swapping sulfate for hydroxide in a hydrotalcite-like CoNi-DABCO framework opens up hydroxyl-rich sites that anchor RuOx domains onto the CoNi backbone through Ru-O-M bridges. The bridge is there to control the sequential dehydrogenation steps that amine-to-nitrile electrooxidation needs, not just to decorate the surface with ruthenium.

original_title: Beyond Thiol-First Chemistry: Thiophosphonium-Gated Activation-State Capture in Disulfide Bioconjugation
title: Catching the disulfide mid-activation, before it even becomes a thiol
blurb: Most disulfide bioconjugation chemistry reduces the bond to free thiols first and only reports on that end state, missing whatever species forms the moment the S-S bond is actually activated. This proposes a thiophosphonium-gated approach to trap that transient activation state directly instead. It's a framework paper, so the real test is whether anyone builds a useful conjugation method on top of it.

original_title: Site-Specific Enzymatic Radiofluorination of Biomolecules: From Current Methodologies to Emerging Opportunities
title: Getting F-18 onto proteins without cooking them first
blurb: A review of enzymatic routes for site-specific F-18 labeling of biomolecules for PET. The problem it's working around: standard radiofluorination wants hot, anhydrous, basic, aprotic conditions, which is exactly what a folded protein can't survive, so enzymes are the fix. No new data here, just a map of where the methods stand and what's still missing.

original_title: Antibody–drug conjugates in hematologic malignancies: from target biology to linker–payload pharmacology and clinical evidence
title: ADCs for blood cancers, start to finish
blurb: A review tracing antibody-drug conjugates in hematologic malignancies from target biology through linker-payload pharmacology to the actual clinical evidence. No new result, just the field laid out in one place.

original_title: Molecular Dominoes
title: The domino chemistry hiding inside every prodrug linker
blurb: A review of self-immolative linkers, the trigger-spacer-cargo setups where removing a protecting group kicks off a cascading fragmentation that releases the drug on its own. The appeal is decoupling activation from release, which matters when a drug's problem is pharmacokinetics, selectivity, or solubility rather than potency.

original_title: Microdosimetry and biological effectiveness of 35 radionuclides for targeted tumor therapy: alpha, beta, and low-energy electron emitters.
title: Thirty-five radionuclides, ranked by how much damage they actually do per decay
blurb: A microdosimetry comparison across alpha, beta, and low-energy electron emitters for targeted tumor therapy, the kind of accounting that matters more than half-life when you're actually picking an isotope. More reference table than news, but a useful one to have in one place.

original_title: Linker Architecture-Guided Design of FAPI Dimers for Improved Pharmacokinetics and FAP-Targeted Theranostics
title: Two FAP inhibitors stapled together, and the linker decides whether it works
blurb: They built a series of FAPI dimers off the UAMC1110 scaffold with different linker architectures, screened them stepwise, and labeled the survivors with 68Ga. The bet is that dimerizing improves pharmacokinetics over the monomer, with linker choice doing most of the actual work in that tradeoff. Still a candidate at the screening stage, not anything dosed in a trial.

original_title: Regio- and Diastereoselective Thiol-ene Click Reaction and Application for the Synthesis of Semicrystalline Polythioethers
title: A thiol-ene reaction that actually picks a side, for once
blurb: Radical thiol-ene addition to internal alkenes is usually sloppy on both regiochemistry and stereochemistry, but this bicyclic lactone alkene reacts with better than 99% regio- and diastereoselectivity across a range of thiols. They then photopolymerize it into genuinely regio- and stereoregular semicrystalline polythioethers, which is the actual payoff: ordered thiol-ene polymers you don't normally get.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Ubiquitination-Informed Reinforcement Learning Linker Generator Enables Discovery of Novel FGFR4 PROTAC Degraders
title: Letting reinforcement learning pick your PROTAC linker
blurb: PotentialLinker uses RL with a weighted harmonic mean score to predict degradation activity and optimize PROTAC linkers without needing a precomputed ternary complex structure. It reproduced known SAR on STAT3/RIPK1 and recommended E3 ligases, then was used to find new FGFR4 degraders. A computational design tool, so whether the picks actually degrade anything in a dish is the part the case studies only gesture at.

original_title: Deferoxamine‐Engineered Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles Unlock High‐Valence Metal Channels for Multiplexed Mass Cytometry
title: More mass tags for mass cytometry, by stuffing nanoparticles with metals nobody else uses
blurb: Deferoxamine-engineered mesoporous silica nanoparticles pack roughly 10,000 atoms each of Zr4+, Hf4+, Nb5+, or Ta5+, metals mass cytometry has mostly ignored, and hold onto them in physiological buffer. PEGylate and conjugate an antibody and you've got new multiplexing channels for a technique that's been bottlenecked by how many mass tags exist.

original_title: Tween 80 reorganizes the chitosan precursor microenvironment to enhance genipin crosslinking and hydrogel performance.
title: A surfactant that makes chitosan hydrogels cross-link better just by being in the way
blurb: Tween 80 reorganizes the chitosan precursor microenvironment before genipin even starts crosslinking, and that reorganization is what improves the resulting hydrogel's performance. A formulation trick more than new chemistry, but a cheap one if it generalizes past this system.

original_title: Click-chemistry targeting of inflammation using NIR-emitting lanthanide nanoparticles with preserved optical functionality
title: Click chemistry bolts a NIR tag onto inflamed blood vessels
blurb: Bioorthogonal click conjugation lets Nd/Yb-doped nanoparticles latch onto VCAM-1 on inflamed endothelial cells, and they keep their near-infrared emission and thermal-sensing readout after being decorated with the targeting handle. Nice that the optics survive the chemistry, but it's cell-level targeting so far, not a living animal.

original_title: Cytotoxic drugs and bispecific T cell engagers synergize to rewire host immunity and elicit polyclonal antitumor T cell responses
title: An ADC that also teaches the immune system the trick
blurb: Pairing the HER2 ADC trastuzumab deruxtecan with HER2-targeted CD28 bispecific antibodies drove durable tumor rejection and lasting immune memory in humanized mice, even in tumors already resistant to the ADC alone. The CD28 bispecific turns a one-shot cytotoxic hit into a polyclonal T cell response that sticks around, mouse data for now.

original_title: Advancing Engineered Living Hydrogels Using Cell-Node Crosslinking.
title: Hydrogels that crosslink through the cells instead of the polymer
blurb: An engineered living hydrogel built around crosslinking at the cell nodes themselves rather than the surrounding matrix. That's the whole pitch here, details are thin beyond the concept.

original_title: Genetic code expansion for site-specific encoding of a switchable, intrinsic fluorophore–quencher pair to monitor protein dynamics
title: A fluorophore-quencher pair you can switch on with light or click chemistry
blurb: Genetic code expansion installs acridonylalanine and methyltetrazinyl phenylalanine as a built-in fluorophore-quencher pair, and either a bioorthogonal or a photochemical reaction on the Tet residue kills the quenching. No external dye needed, just flip the switch and watch protein dynamics light up.

original_title: QuickXL: An Open-source Ultraviolet Irradiation Device with Programmable Exposure and Active Cooling for Nucleic Acid Crosslinking
title: A DIY UV rig for crosslinking RNA
blurb: QuickXL is an open-source irradiation box, 24 LEDs at 365-370 nm split into two switchable arrays, with a microcontroller running programmable exposure timing, active cooling and an OLED display, built for psoralen-mediated RNA photocrosslinking. The point is getting reproducible UV dosing without buying a commercial crosslinker.

original_title: Diastereoselective Alkylation of Tryptophan and Tryptophan-Containing Peptides via Cooperative Rh(II)/Chiral Phosphoric Acid Catalysis
title: One catalyst pair, two different spots on tryptophan
blurb: Cooperative Rh(II)/chiral phosphoric acid catalysis alkylates tryptophan and Trp-containing peptides at up to 99:1 dr, and which carbon reacts is substrate-controlled: bare tryptophan alkylates at N1, but preinstall a phenyl group at C2 and the selectivity flips to C6. Mild, low catalyst loading, and it works on peptides, which is the part worth caring about for late-stage modification.

original_title: Prostate-Specific Membrane Antigen-Targeted Radioligand Therapy in Prostate Cancer: Patient Selection, Treatment Workflow, and Emerging Directions.
title: A field guide to PSMA radioligand therapy
blurb: A review walking through patient selection, treatment workflow, and where PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy in prostate cancer is headed next. No new data, just the practice rundown.
venue: Magn Reson Imaging Clin N Am

original_title: Fully automated [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 radiosynthesis using GalliAd(®) generator and MiniAIO(®) synthesizer: development and validation for PET imaging of fibroblast activation protein.
title: Push-button Ga-68 FAPI-46 for FAP PET scans
blurb: Fully automated radiosynthesis of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 off a GalliAd generator and MiniAIO synthesizer, developed and validated for imaging fibroblast activation protein. Unglamorous but this is the kind of automation that decides whether a tracer stays a research curiosity or actually gets used in the clinic.

original_title: Synthesis and reactivity of a dimetallocarbene
title: A carbon atom bonded to just two metals, finally made
blurb: Carbon bound to four metals at once has been known for a while, but a carbene with a divalent carbon pinned between just two, one PdII and one AuI, had stayed elusive until now. The singlet ground state sits close enough to the triplet that the thing reacts with almost anything: C(sp3)-H bonds, radical H transfer, CO, CO2, phenyl disulfide. That ambiphilic range is the actual headline.

original_title: Buried Interfacial Transport Governs Oxide-Protected Electrocatalysis
title: What's actually happening at the oxide layer protecting your catalyst
blurb: Oxide overlayers protect electrocatalysts the way graphene does, but unlike graphene they create a buried metal-oxide interface that separates where protons go in from where product comes out. Proton transport through that oxide has been studied to death; whether the product that forms there leaves as an H2 molecule or as an H atom has stayed a live argument, and this work goes after that buried interface directly.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Irradiation‐Wavelength‐Tuned Stepwise [2+2] Cycloaddition of Indolylphenylpropenone Derivatives as a Platform for Light–Mechanical Energy Conversion
title: Wavelength picks which cyclobutane you get, in the crystal itself
blurb: Indolylphenylpropenone crystals run a stepwise [2+2] cycloaddition where the light's color, not a catalyst, decides which cyclobutane isomer forms, blue light giving one kind of monocyclobutane. The pitch is light-to-mechanical energy conversion, with the crystal's own prearrangement doing the regio- and stereocontrol that's normally the hard part of [2+2] chemistry.

original_title: Time to maximal response of trastuzumab deruxtecan in patients with HER2-Positive metastatic breast cancer: A multicenter retrospective study (TRACE)
title: How long before trastuzumab deruxtecan actually peaks
blurb: A retrospective multicenter study (TRACE) pulling real-world HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer patients on T-DXd from 2020-2025 to measure time to maximal response, something trial data hasn't nailed down. The number matters for deciding how long to run induction before switching to maintenance, but it's chart review, not a trial.

original_title: Lu]Lu-PSMA Radiopharmaceutical Therapy: International Survey of 102 Theranostic Centers - Journal of Nuclear Medicine
title: Asking 102 clinics how they're actually running Lu-PSMA therapy
blurb: A straight survey across 102 theranostic centers worldwide on how they administer Lu-177-PSMA radioligand therapy, practice variation rather than a trial result. Useful mostly as a snapshot of how uneven the field's protocols still are.

original_title: Click-Functionalizable Tetrathiafulvalene-Tetrathiolate Diradicaloids as Modular NIR-II Fluorophores
title: Click chemistry turns a NIR-II dye into a build-it-yourself kit
blurb: Tetrathiafulvalene-tetrathiolate bimetallic diradicaloid complexes already get bright NIR-II emission with quantum yields that beat most NIR-II fluorophores, and now carry click handles so you can bolt on whatever targeting chemistry you need. Modular is the point here, not a new emission mechanism.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Hijacking Prenyltransferases and Terpene Synthases for the Enzymatic Synthesis of Non‐natural C 19 , C 24 , and C 29 Terpenoids
title: Feeding terpene enzymes a demethylated building block and letting them improvise
blurb: Strip a methyl group off farnesyl pyrophosphate and run it through the normal elongation enzymes (GGPP/GFPP synthases) and then 30 downstream diterpene and sesterterpene synthases, and out come 24 new terpenoid skeletons at odd carbon counts nature doesn't build. The fun part is that in two cases the enzymes misfired across the GGPP/GFPP boundary and made nor-sesterterpenes anyway, meaning they're less picky about substrate length than assumed.

original_title: Targeting Highly Reactive Oxygen Species for Prodrug Activation Using the CReKT Approach II: The Effect of Aryl Substitution on Release Kinetics
title: Tuning how fast a ROS-triggered prodrug dumps its payload
blurb: Follow-up on their hypochlorite-triggered prodrug system (thioether oxidizes to sulfoxide, then an intramolecular attack on an ester releases the payload), this time running 17 aryl-substituted analogs to map how substituent electronics change release kinetics. Still a rate-tuning exercise on the bench, not biology yet, but it's the knob you'd need before this becomes a usable ROS-activated prodrug.

original_title: Rewriting Copper-Catalyzed ATRA Reactions through a Cu(II)/Cu(III) Pathway
title: A Cu(II) catalyst that skips the usual Cu(I) middleman
blurb: ATRA reactions normally run on a photocatalytic Cu(I)/Cu(II) cycle, with Cu(II) complexes usually just sitting around as precursors. This [Cu(dpc)OAc] complex is dead in the reactions Cu(II) usually handles but turns out to catalyze ATRA, like alkene chlorosulfonylation, apparently through a Cu(II)/Cu(III) pathway instead. Rewrites which oxidation states are actually doing the work.

original_title: Enantioselective Intramolecular 1,2-Alkoxyphosphinoylation of 4-Aryl-homoallyl Alcohols Catalyzed by Chiral Oxidovanadium Complexes
title: Chiral vanadium catalysts talk radicals into picking one enantiomer
blurb: Intramolecular radical cyclization is usually hard to make enantioselective, but chiral oxidovanadium complexes with N-salicylidene-tert-butylglycinate ligands pull it off on homoallyl alcohol substrates, the beta-hydroxyethyl-styrene version in acetonitrile working best. Output is 3-diphenylphosphinoyl tetrahydrofurans in yields up to 82%, a stereocontrolled route to a ring system that's normally a pain to make this way.

original_title: Synthesis of Enones and Enals From Alkenes via Alkenyl Thianthrenium Salts
title: Thianthrenium salts turn alkenes into stereodefined enones and enals
blurb: Alkenyl thianthrenium salts act as bench-stable, stereodefined alkenyl electrophiles that slot into Pd-catalyzed carbonylative couplings: pair with in-situ alkylzincs for a carbonylative Negishi and you get enones, swap in triethylsilane for a reductive version and you get enals. Same electrophile pool, two different carbonyl products depending on what you pair it with.

original_title: Enhanced Immunocomplex Immunogenicity Enables Isolation of an Anti-immunocomplex Nanobody for Noncompetitive Detection of Microcystins
title: Getting a nanobody to recognize the antibody-toxin handshake itself
blurb: Small-molecule immunoassays are usually stuck in competitive format because the analyte can't bind two antibodies at once. They boosted the immunogenicity of the antibody-microcystin immunocomplex and ran competitive phage display against it to pull out an anti-immunocomplex nanobody, letting microcystin detection go noncompetitive with a direct positive readout. The hard part, as usual with these reagents, is avoiding ones that also bind the bare antibody when it isn't holding anything.

original_title: eHydrogenation: Pd/C-Catalyzed Reduction of Alkenes and Alkynes without an External H2 Supply
title: Hydrogenation without the H2 tank
blurb: Commercial Pd/C paired with plain constant-current electrolysis reduces alkenes and alkynes in ethanol at room temperature, in air, no hydrazine or bespoke electrocatalyst needed. 0.5 mol% Pd tolerates halides, nitriles, benzyl ethers, and free alcohols, and they got a flow version running too. Nice if your fume hood just doesn't have a H2 line.

original_title: Spiroselenopyrans: Reversible Light- and Soft-Acid-Triggered Switching of Spirocyclic C–Se Bonds
title: Swapping sulfur for selenium in spiropyran switches
blurb: Spiropyrans are the go-to photoswitch scaffold, but putting a heavier chalcogen at the spiro carbon usually just gets you a benzoselenophene instead of a switch, since that's the side reaction it wants to collapse into. Steric bulk engineered into the design blocks that path, opening up a whole family of selenium-centered spiropyrans rather than one lucky derivative.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Liquid-Phase Deep Carbon Elongation from C1 to Crystalline Graphite
title: Turning chloromethane into graphite in a beaker
blurb: A Lewis-acid-boosted triflic acid medium, TfOH/Hg(OTf)2, chews through chloromethane solvent and builds the carbons back up, coupling by coupling, into condensed hydrocarbons and eventually crystalline graphitic flakes, all in one pot in solution. Getting from single carbons to an extended sp2 lattice without a furnace or vapor deposition is the odd part; the mercury triflate is clearly doing the heavy lifting most routes would need much harsher conditions for.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Oxetane-to-Cyclopropane Skeletal Editing through Oxygen Deletion
title: Deleting an oxygen to turn an oxetane into a cyclopropane
blurb: Blue light with iodoform and DMF generates a Vilsmeier-Haack reagent that pries the oxetane open into a diiodide, then zinc closes the ring back up minus the oxygen, landing on a cyclopropane. Catalyst-free, broad functional-group tolerance, works on late-stage substrates, and the mechanistic evidence points to a fast radical cyclization doing the actual ring closure.

original_title: CBr4-Mediated Photodriven Synthesis of Quinolin-2(1 H )-ones from o -Alkynylaryl Isocyanides via Tandem Radical Reactions
title: One-pot radical cascade to quinolinones, courtesy of CBr4 and visible light
blurb: Visible-light photoredox pushes o-alkynylaryl isocyanides and CBr4 through addition, cyclization, elimination, and isomerization in a single pot to give quinolin-2(1H)-ones. The mechanism runs through a brominated quinoline intermediate, and both the O2 and the water they deliberately add turn out to be necessary rather than just along for the ride.

original_title: Sequential Flow Assembly of Unsymmetrical Triaryl Architectures via Aryllithium Interception
title: Taming aryllithiums long enough to actually use them, in flow
blurb: Aryllithiums are brutally reactive and hard to control in a flask, so this is a catalyst-free flow setup that does halogen-lithium exchange with n-BuLi and traps the intermediate electrophilically before it can misbehave, with residence time standing in for a catalyst. That lets them hit bifunctional electrophiles selectively at just the carbonyl, building unsymmetrical triaryl products batch chemistry struggles with.

original_title: From Divergence to Coupling: Interfacial Water and Adsorbed Hydrogen during Hydrogen Evolution
title: Watching water and adsorbed hydrogen trade places on platinum, mid-HER
blurb: Using Dynamic Response Spectroscopy, which can actually separate interfacial signal from diffusion-layer noise, they track how interfacial water and adsorbed H* on platinum shift together as the potential drops from 0.4 V. Three distinct regions turn up, each defined by a different dominant interfacial process, which is more mechanistic resolution on hydrogen evolution than the usual appeal to "water structure."

original_title: A Nanoscale Valley Sink Governs Temperature-Dependent Catalytic Selectivity on Corrugated Iron Carbide
title: Why a bumpy iron carbide surface flips which polymer it makes with temperature
blurb: Neural-network-accelerated molecular dynamics plus DFT and microkinetics trace a temperature-dependent ethylene polymerization switch on corrugated Fe3C back to something static, single-site barriers can't capture: how fast dissociated hydrogen atoms clear out of the surface's nanoscale valleys. Temperature sets that clearance rate, and the clearance rate, not a fixed activation energy, is what actually decides the product.

original_title: Enantioselective synthesis of sulfondiimidoyl fluorides via pyridine- N -oxide-catalyzed sulfondiimidoyl transfer
title: A chiral catalyst for sulfondiimidoyl fluorides worth keeping the stereocenter on
blurb: Chlorination gives racemic sulfondiimidoyl chlorides, then a chiral pyridine-N-oxide catalyst runs an asymmetric Cl-F exchange with TMAF as the fluoride source, up to 90% yield and 92% ee, through what looks like a dynamic kinetic asymmetric transformation rather than plain resolution. They follow up with SuFEx clicks using C, O, and N nucleophiles, so the products aren't just sitting there being chiral for no reason.

original_title: Biofluid-Triggered Ferrocene-Hyaluronic Acid Hydrogel with Programmed Rigid-to-Flexible Transition for Synergistic Hemostasis and Postoperative Adhesion Prevention.
title: A wound hydrogel that starts stiff and softens once it's done its job
blurb: A ferrocene-hyaluronic acid hydrogel triggered by biofluid to switch from rigid to flexible on a schedule: stiff first to control bleeding, then soft to keep tissues from sticking together as they heal. Neat idea if the timing holds up as cleanly as the name suggests.

original_title: Palladium-Catalyzed Intermolecular Dehydrogenative Homodimerization of Six-Membered Cyclic Tertiary Anilines
title: One-pot fusion of two anilines into a nitrogen heterocycle, four C–H bonds at once
blurb: A palladium catalyst dimerizes six-membered tertiary N-arylanilines by snapping four C–H bonds in one step, building the fused heterocycle skeleton directly instead of piecing it together. Kinetic isotope effect work pins the slow step on the aliphatic C–H cleavage, with a Pd(II)/Pd(IV) cycle proposed. Tolerates both electron-rich and electron-poor aryl groups, so the scope looks genuine.

original_title: Photoredox synthesis of 4-cyanoalkyl-4 H -3,1-benzoxazines via iminyl-radical C–C cleavage
title: Photoredox radicals snap a C–C bond to build cyano-benzoxazines
blurb: An iminyl radical fragments a C–C bond and the pieces reassemble into 4-cyanoalkyl benzoxazines, up to 81% yield across a decent substrate range. Mostly notable for showing iminyl-radical C–C cleavage can be steered into a useful cascade rather than just blowing the molecule apart.

original_title: Joint single-cell capture of Cas9 edits and transcriptomes reveals on- and off-target effects on gene expression
title: Reading a cell's CRISPR edits and its transcriptome at once
blurb: Superb-seq bolts T7 in situ transcription onto scRNA-seq so you get the actual Cas9 edit and the resulting expression changes from the same single cell, instead of inferring one from the other. That lets it tie off-target cuts directly to the expression fallout they cause, not just flag that they happened.

original_title: A DNA–organocatalyst hybrid for aqueous asymmetric aldol reaction via asymmetric activation/poisoning
title: A DNA leash turns a racemic catalyst asymmetric by poisoning half of it
blurb: Hooking a racemic organocatalyst to DNA lets one enantiomer get activated while the other gets selectively poisoned, pulling off an asymmetric aldol reaction in water. The practical win is screening, down from three variables to two, which is the kind of thing that actually gets used rather than admired.

original_title: Ligand-Coupled Electron Transfer Enables Highly Stable Two-Electron Electrochemical Energy Storage using a Nickel Bis(diphosphine) Complex
title: Squeezing a two-electron battery reaction into one redox step
blurb: A nickel bis(diphosphine) complex normally gives two separate one-electron redox events, but dosing in chloride or bromide plus excess dppe ligand shifts a halide-coordination equilibrium and compresses the two steps to under 100 mV apart, close enough to act like a clean 2-electron transfer. The equilibrium constants involved are tiny (K_Br = 0.015), so it's a delicate trick, but it's a real lever on matching redox potentials for energy storage.

original_title: Light-Driven Active Transport across a Liquid Membrane via Photoswitch Sensitization
title: Pumping molecules across a membrane with just one light source
blurb: Photoswitch-driven active transport usually needs light hitting the two sides of the membrane differently, which falls apart once the membrane goes nanoscale. Parking a ruthenium sensitizer in one compartment lets a single light source generate different photostationary states on each side anyway, so the asymmetry comes from where the sensitizer sits rather than from the illumination setup.

original_title: Encapsulating an iron complex within a heme and anthraquinone codecorated capsule for multiphoton C(sp3)−H bond oxygenation
title: A light-switchable cage that mimics allosteric enzymes for C–H oxidation
blurb: A non-heme FeIII complex sits caged inside a capsule co-decorated with heme and anthraquinone, and light flips the bridged FeIII-porphyrin pair into an unbridged FeII/O=FeIV state that does the actual C(sp3)-H oxygenation chemistry. The point is getting a synthetic system to switch its catalytic state on demand like an allosterically regulated enzyme, rather than just sitting there permanently active.

original_title: Universal charge-tag labelling of undetectable polymers for mass spectrometric characterization
title: Giving invisible-to-MS hydrocarbons a charge so they finally show up
blurb: High molecular weight aliphatic hydrocarbons are basically a blind spot for ESI-MS, since they barely ionize, so petroleomics has mostly settled for fingerprinting just the polar fraction of oil. This is a charge-tag derivatization aimed at dragging the nonpolar fraction into view too, extending a trick that already works on other compound classes to the one that's resisted it.

original_title: Boron-complexed oxidized dextran/carboxymethyl chitosan hydrogel loaded with paeoniflorin alleviates UC via TLR4-NF-κB pathway regulation and intestinal mucosal barrier restoration.
title: A boron-crosslinked hydrogel delivers paeoniflorin straight to inflamed gut
blurb: An oxidized dextran/carboxymethyl chitosan hydrogel, held together with boron crosslinks, carries paeoniflorin to treat ulcerative colitis by damping TLR4-NF-κB signaling and patching up the intestinal mucosal barrier.

original_title: Aza-Henry Reactions of Cyclic Nitrones En Route to 2 H -Imidazole-Tethered Nitrogen Heterocycles
title: Turning nitrones into nitrile oxide precursors for new bis-azaheterocycles
blurb: DBU strips the oxygen off 2H-imidazole N-oxides while bolting on nitromethyl groups, and a further step converts those into alpha-chlorooximes, stand-ins for reactive nitrile oxides used to stitch together bis-azaheterocycle scaffolds. Turned up 28 previously unknown compounds, so mostly a scope-building exercise in heterocycle space.

original_title: Silver‐Catalyzed Deacylative Carbonylation of Methyl Ketones to Synthesize Alkyl Heterocyclic Ketones
title: Breaking a methyl ketone apart to rebuild it with CO
blurb: Carbonylation usually struggles with aliphatic ketones because the C-C bonds holding the alkyl chain to the carbonyl don't want to break selectively. A silver catalyst does the deacylative cleavage anyway, swapping the acyl group out and rebuilding it with CO to deliver alkyl heterocyclic ketones, exactly the building blocks everyone wants and nobody wanted to make this way.

original_title: Phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover enables rate-matched nitrate-sulfate paired electrolysis for ammonium persulfate synthesis
title: Finally syncing the two mismatched halves of paired nitrate electrolysis
blurb: Turning nitrate-contaminated wastewater into ammonium persulfate by paired electrolysis keeps stalling on a timing problem: nitrate reduction and sulfate oxidation run at different speeds. A phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover at a PdP2@Cu3P interface gets the two rates to match, letting the whole thing run as direct electrosynthesis instead of two half-cells fighting each other.

original_title: De Novo Design of C-H Hydroxylation Enzymes with Programmed Selectivities
title: Designing C-H oxidation enzymes from scratch instead of evolving them
blurb: Getting a P450-style metalloenzyme to selectively hit one C-H bond normally takes rounds of discovery and directed evolution. Here they start from just a Cys-ligated heme and the right catalytic side chains and compute their way straight to selective C-H hydroxylation biocatalysts with programmed selectivity. If that generalizes, it's a real shortcut around the usual enzyme-engineering slog.

original_title: Mechanically tunable and matrix metalloproteinase responsive hyaluronic acid hydrogel for patient-derived colorectal cancer organoid culture.
title: A hyaluronic acid gel built to degrade like real tumor tissue
blurb: A hyaluronic acid hydrogel for growing patient-derived colorectal cancer organoids, with tunable stiffness and sensitivity to matrix metalloproteinases so it breaks down the way actual tumor matrix does rather than sitting there inert. Not much else to go on, but getting the mechanics right matters a lot for whether organoids behave like the tumor they came from.

original_title: Boron‐Stabilized Diradicaloids of Chichibabin and Müller Hydrocarbons and Their Extended Analogues
title: Stretching out a boron-capped diradical doesn't bring the spins closer
blurb: Boron-stabilized versions of the Chichibabin and Müller diradicals, extended with longer conjugated bridges to see what happens to the two radical centers. The longer the bridge, the weaker the coupling: diradical character climbs from 0.53 to 0.99 and the singlet-triplet gap narrows as you stretch it out. A useful dial, just not the direction you'd want if you needed the spins talking to each other.

original_title: Electrochemical Hydrocarboxylation of Unactivated Alkyl Alkenes
title: Getting CO2 onto alkenes that don't want to be reduced
blurb: Electrochemical hydrocarboxylation usually needs an activated alkene to stabilize the key intermediate, since both the alkene and CO2 have reduction potentials that work against you otherwise. This one does the hydrocarboxylation directly on unactivated alkyl alkenes, no prefunctionalization needed, which is the part that's actually been blocking this route to alkyl carboxylic acids.

original_title: Copper-Mediated Bromodeboronation of Alkenyl Pinacol Boronates: Scope and Stereochemical Outcome
title: Swapping boronate for bromide on alkenes with plain CuBr2
blurb: CuBr2 in wet THF converts alkenyl pinacol boronates straight to the corresponding bromides, 35-90% yield across acyclic and four- to seven-membered ring systems, scales to multigram, and shrugs off Boc amines, ethers, sulfones, fluorines, esters, even a free carboxylic acid. It balks at flexible boronates carrying a nucleophile or an allylic bromide, so know your substrate before you commit.

original_title: Plug-and-Play 3D-Printed Pd Catalytic Cartridges by FFF Printing for Liquid-Phase Organic Synthesis
title: A Pd catalyst cartridge you print instead of weigh out
blurb: FFF 3D printing is normally just prototyping plastic, not catalyst hardware, but here the printed part is the catalyst scaffold: Pd deposited onto a printed polyamide mesh gives a reusable cartridge that snaps into a holder for liquid-phase reactions. Performance tracks the printed topology, so the mesh geometry is doing real catalytic work, not just holding the metal in place.

original_title: Enantioselective Rh-catalyzed addition of indoles to enones and the key role of the free N–H group with acyclic enones
title: Free indole N-H helps, not hurts, this Rh-catalyzed coupling
blurb: Protecting the indole N-H is usually step one before running metal-catalyzed C-C coupling, but this Rh-catalyzed asymmetric conjugate addition of indole boronic acids to acyclic enones runs better with it left free, up to 96% yield and >99:1 e.r., reaching every position on the indole's carbocyclic ring. Leaving the N-H alone is apparently what's doing the work for the selectivity, not just a step saved.

original_title: Aqueous phenazine catholytes mediate efficient hydrogenation at an aqueous–organic interface
title: Phenazine mediators push hydrogenation to the water-organic boundary
blurb: Mediated electrosynthesis keeps running into mediators that aren't stable or tunable enough to be useful. Phenazine redox mediators get nitro compounds hydrogenated right at an aqueous-organic interface, under mild conditions and at substrate concentrations higher than these setups usually handle.

original_title: Engineering peroxygenases for pharmaceutical applications: recent advances and future perspectives
title: Peroxygenases get an engineering makeover for making drugs
blurb: A roundup of where peroxygenase engineering stands for pharmaceutical oxyfunctionalization, the pitch being a greener way to install oxygen than the usual stoichiometric oxidants. It's a perspectives piece surveying progress rather than reporting a new enzyme, so treat it as a map of the field, not a result.

original_title: Piezocatalytic in situ production and utilization of hydrogen peroxide
title: Squeezing crystals to make your own hydrogen peroxide
blurb: A review of piezocatalytic H2O2 production, where mechanical force on piezoelectric materials drives the oxygen reduction and water oxidation half-reactions to make peroxide on site instead of shipping it in. Covers the mechanisms, materials and tweaks to them, and the pitch for disinfection, water treatment, resistance control and therapy. Breadth over a single number, since it's a perspective, not a new material.

original_title: Metal-Centered Spin-State Switching Promotes Stereodivergent Synthesis of E - and Z -Allylamines
title: Spin state decides whether you get E or Z allylamines
blurb: Same weak-field bipyridine ligand, same reaction, but swap the metal's spin state and the stereochemistry of allylic amination flips: high-spin Ni gives E-allylamines, low-spin Pd gives Z, and Fe, Rh and Ir track the same pattern. Spin as the actual steering handle for stereoselectivity, not the ligand tinkering catalysis papers usually reach for.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Expanding Chemical Space Enables Data–Driven Structure–Activity Relationships in Cage Catalysis
title: Data-driven SAR finally comes to cage catalysis
blurb: Bioinspired cage catalysis has mostly relied on DFT run over a handful of near-identical cages, because the known chemical space was too thin to support real structure-activity relationships. This builds out that chemical space and sets up a data-driven framework instead, aimed at the mechanistic insight that DFT-on-a-few-cages can't scale to.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: A Mirror-Image L-RNA Aptamer Targeting Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-1α Promoter G-Quadruplex Potentiates Tumor Radiotherapy In Vivo
title: A mirror-image aptamer that disarms tumors' radiation resistance
blurb: Mirror-image SELEX turns up an L-RNA aptamer, L-Apt5-4, that folds into a stem loop and binds the G-quadruplex sitting in HIF-1α's own promoter with high affinity, then gets into the nucleus. Blocking that hypoxia pathway makes tumors respond better to radiotherapy in vivo. Being L-RNA should also make it nuclease-resistant, which is presumably the point of going mirror-image in the first place.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: GPC3-Targeted sdAb-PET Imaging of Hepatocellular Carcinoma with Single-Domain Antibody Tracers
title: Nanobody PET tracers for spotting liver cancer by its GPC3
blurb: Two GPC3-targeted PET probes built on the nanobody G6, one plain and one fused to an albumin-binding domain to keep it circulating longer, both radiolabeled with gallium-68 and tested in GPC3-positive HCC models. The albumin fusion is the bet that you can buy nanobodies more imaging time without giving up their usual fast clearance and tissue penetration.

original_title: Generative AI Enables Rapid Point-of-Care Diagnostics via Signal Prediction in Pre-equilibrium Immunoassays
title: Skipping the wait in immunoassays by having AI guess the ending
blurb: Normal immunoassays make you wait hours to hit equilibrium before you can trust the reading. This version tracks the early motion of magnetic nanoparticles on a microfluidic chip and has an AI model infer what the equilibrium signal would have been from that early trajectory. Clever if the inference generalizes past whatever conditions it was trained on, which point-of-care use will stress pretty quickly.

original_title: Anchoring Sites for Gold in Zeolites and Ethanol Selective Oxidation Over Zeolite‐Supported Gold Catalysts
title: Where gold actually sits inside a zeolite, and why it changes ethanol oxidation
blurb: Combined experiments and calculations map how Au anchors inside ZSM-5, mordenite and faujasite, mostly by displacing a proton from either an Al site or a silanol group, and compared against silicalite-1, silica and silica-alumina. Loading, Si/Al ratio and framework topology all shift which anchor sites dominate, and that anchoring, not just how much gold you load, is what ends up setting selectivity in ethanol's oxidation to gas-phase O2.
